Hi Oliver / Aisha —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side to make sure we’re aligned and to capture action items:

Key pain points you described:
- Real-time clinical decisioning needs (<200ms) for short prompts used in triage flows
- Throughput spikes during morning sync window (~4x baseline for 20–30 minutes)
- Data residency and PHI controls for diagnostic notes

Primary goals:
1) P95 inference latency under 120ms for the 128-token typical prompt (goal: <100ms for demo)
2) Sustained baseline throughput of ~120 requests/min with 2x burst handling
3) End-to-end encrypted storage + KMS integration for request logging and audit trails

Technical summary / what we recommend:
- Model: start with an Llama-3 13B quantized variant (8-bit) for parity on hallucination rates, fallback to 7B quantized for extreme burst mode.
- Topology: Dedicated pool in us-west-2 with a small private VPC peering for PHI; route non-PHI traffic to hosted reservoir for cheaper capacity.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache for common triage prompts to reduce token compute by ~20–40%.
- Batching: request-aware continuous batching with a 30ms aggregation window to balance latency and throughput.
- Fallbacks: automated model variant fallback + cross-region failover if latency SLOs are at risk.

Open questions we flagged on the call:
- Do you expect attachments or long-context documents to be part of the triage path ( >1k tokens )?
- Procurement timeline & SOC2 evidence needed for a pilot contract (Marissa / procurement thread below).

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- Rishi: formal capacity estimate and cost delta for dedicated pool vs hosted burst — attached (carelogic_capacity_estimate.xlsx). ETA: EOD Fri (5/21).
- Marissa: send a draft mutual action plan and procurement checklist. ETA: Mon 5/24.
- Neha: architecture sketch for VPC deployment + recommended SLOs. ETA: Mon 5/24.
- Oliver / Aisha: confirm whether triage flows will accept a 30ms batching window in the happy path; confirm procurement contact.

Attachments: carelogic_capacity_estimate.xlsx (capacity / cost sketch)

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up demo if helpful.

—

Thanks Rishi — this is a helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- The triage prompts are typically short (60–200 tokens) for initial routing. We do have a separate path where clinicians can paste notes (~1.5k tokens); that would be an outlier but needs consideration for routing.
- 30ms batching sounds fine for the triage path, as long as spikes are handled without violating the 120ms p95. For clinician-paste flows, we expect higher latency and would prefer async processing.
- Procurement: we’re on a tight timeline and are aiming to have a pilot agreement signed by mid-June. I’ve looped procurement@carelogic.ai to get visibility on required SOC2 docs and any security questionnaires.

Can you flag any blockers on PHI handling for the VPC approach? Also, any preliminary estimate on monthly cost for a dedicated pool sized for our baseline + bursts would help our planning.

Hi all — following up with the technical details we discussed. I’m attaching a quick topology sketch (topology_sketch.png) and a short answers list for procurement.

Short answers for procurement / security pack:
- PHI handling: Private VPC deployment with customer-managed KMS (HSM option available) for encryption of logs & stored artifacts. No raw inference payloads are persisted in host logs by default.
- SOC2: we will provide the attestation PDF and a runbook excerpt showing access controls & rotation policies.
- Audit logs: token-level traces can be stored in your S3 bucket with server-side encryption and IAM roles; redact policy available.

Technical SLOs and deployment guidance (recommendation):
- Latency SLOs: P50 < 60ms, P95 < 120ms for 128-token triage prompts (measured at application ingress). For clinician long-text flows (>1k tokens) treat as async — no hard p95 requirement.
- Throughput baseline: target sustained 120 req/min (~2 req/s). Peak burst: up to 480 req/min for 20–30 minutes. We’d size a dedicated pool with ~6 accelerated instances (quantized 13B) to cover baseline + cache hit assumptions; this sizing assumes ~30% KV cache hit for triage prompts.
- Batching params: continuous batching with 20–30ms aggregation window; dynamic batch sizing up to 32 sequences depending on request length.
- Cache strategy: prefix cache for canonical triage prompts; separate KV cache per model variant to avoid cold-starts on fallbacks.
- Fallback plan: automated model variant fallback to 7B quantized (lower cost) with monitored quality checks; cross-region read-only fallback if us-west capacity is saturated.

Operational notes:
- Canary / rollout: start with 5% traffic to dedicated pool for 48 hours, monitor token-level latency and output quality on a labeled prompt set (we can help set up eval runs).
- Monitoring hooks: we’ll expose per-route latency histograms and token-level cost breakdowns to your dashboard and provide alerting for SLO breaches.

Attachments: topology_sketch.png (simple VPC + peering diagram)

If you want, I can turn the sizing notes into a short one-pager for procurement. If that works I’ll drop it by EOD Monday.
